children: The European Commission sent a statement of objections Wednesday to China's MMG over its planned $500M purchase of Anglo American's
Brazilian nickel business, saying the acquisition could divert low-carbon ferronickel supply away from Europe.
The European Union's executive arm said it is concerned that MMG could divert its supplies away from European producers, potentially impacting prices and hampering local stainless steel makers.

The Commission noted that China Minmetals, MMG's majority owner, is controlled by the China's state-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission, which controls major stainless steel producers of its own.

The warning ramped up ​pressure on MMG to offer concessions in return for clearance of the deal after remedies offered during the Commission's preliminary review were rejected for not sufficiently addressing concerns.
said it was disappointed with the Commission's warning, adding that the deal would maintain the number of ferronickel suppliers ​in the market.

title: European Union issues antitrust warning over MMG's nickel deal with Anglo American
